To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured electric breakdowns in argon gas and liquid argon at atmospheric pressure, and that the breakdown voltage in argon liquid is about 10 times lower than in gas.
the dielectric strength in liquid argon is about 100 kV/cm for distances larger than 1 cm.
liquid argon is a very good insulator at centimeter scale and that it is possible to build LAr TPCs with a breakdown-free high voltage feed-through.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new generation of LAr TPCs for neutrino physics experiments.
the design of the liquid argon ionization detectors for neutrino physics, in particular the LArTPC.
the study of electric breakdown in liquid argon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the breakdown voltage of liquid argon is 40 kV per cm, and the breakdown-free operation of LArTPCs is achievable at 50 kV/cm.
the breakdown voltage in liquid argon is in the 40 kV range, with a 20 kV uncertainty, for a 40 mm gap.
the electric field strength in liquid argon is not sufficient to produce breakdowns, even in the presence of impurities and contaminants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the breakdowns are observed for electric field strengths as low as 20 kV/cm and the flash-overs occur for applied voltages as low as 55 kV for a length of the ribbed dielectrics of 300 mm.
liquid argon is a good candidate for the construction of large-scale TPCs, as it is a cheap, easy-to-handle and safe medium.
the breakdown field in liquid argon is about one third the breakdown field in the same gas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dielectric strength is much lower than expected from the extrapolation of the data available in literature for distances below 1 mm.
a breakdown-free operation of a TPC is possible only with a cathode-anode distance of at least 10 mm.

the dielectric of the feed-through should be made of a material with a breakdown voltage higher than 55 kV.
